title: Homecoming and Locker
premise: Rosalind 'Ros' Winterbourne, a trans coder hiding behind an anonymous account that documents every secret at Halloway Prep, counts the days to graduation like a sentence. When he finds coded directions in his late grandmother's recipe box, he discovers she ran 'the Locker,' an underground network that once protected the school's outcasts — and that someone is using it now, twisting it into a tool of blackmail and control. As Ros rebuilds the Locker with a found family of misfits, he must expose the corrupt student council president who weaponized his own anonymous account against him, and finally decide who to be when the labels come off: at graduation's final audition, Ros performs under his real name, having chosen belonging over invisibility.
about_author: Jude Quintana is a former high school debate coach who writes stories about kids who find their people in the unlikeliest corners. They live in a small apartment full of houseplants and half-finished manuscripts, and they believe every recipe box hides something.

chapters.title: Ninety-Three Days
chapters.summary: Ros's POV. Opening on day ninety-three until graduation, we meet Ros coding in the library basement and posting as @hallowayghost, an anonymous account that knows everyone's secrets. The emotional beat is suffocating invisibility: Ros is safe online and erased everywhere else, counting days like a sentence.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Ros's POV. Sorting his grandmother's belongings, Ros finds her recipe box — but one card contains coordinates, a cipher key, and the word LOCKER. The beat is eerie wonder; grief curdles into curiosity as Ros realizes grandma left him instructions, not ingredients.

chapters.title: Decoded
chapters.summary: Ros's POV, intercut with forum posts from @hallowayghost. Cracking the cipher reveals the Locker: a hidden room beneath the old gym where his grandmother once sheltered Halloway's outcasts. The beat is revelation — Ros inherits a legacy he never knew existed.

chapters.title: The Room Beneath
chapters.summary: Ros's POV. Ros breaks into the Locker and finds decades of letters, photos, and a ledger of names — including students the school erased. Someone has been here recently. The beat is haunted awe turning to unease: the past isn't finished with Halloway.

chapters.title: People Who Don't Fit
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotating through Marisol (runaway artist), Dev (expelled debater), and June (quiet athlete). Ros cautiously recruits them, showing each a piece of the Locker. The beat is tentative connection — strangers recognizing themselves in each other for the first time.

chapters.title: Rules of the House
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The group drafts new rules for the revived Locker: no blackmail, no hierarchies, no one gets erased. But they discover recent entries in the ledger written in fresh ink. The beat is idealism shadowed by dread — someone else is already using the room.

chapters.title: The President's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Investigating, Dev discovers student council president Cassius Vane has been logging secrets in the Locker's style — and trading them for favors. The beat is cold anger; the sanctuary has been corrupted into a weapon.

chapters.title: @hallowayghost Exposed
chapters.summary: Ros's POV. Cassius leaks that @hallowayghost attends Halloway, turning the whole school into hunters. Ros watches classmates speculate viciously about who the ghost might be. The beat is terror and betrayal — his shield becomes a target.

chapters.title: What the Ghost Knows
chapters.summary: June's POV. Cassius privately confronts June, revealing he knows the ghost's identity and offering protection in exchange for spying on the group. The beat is agonizing pressure; June must choose between safety and the first friends she's ever had.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Letters
chapters.summary: Ros's POV. Reading grandma's letters in the Locker, Ros learns she was expelled for protecting a student in 1978 — and that she kept writing to the school's lost kids for forty years. The beat is fierce inheritance: Ros understands what he's fighting for.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. June's odd behavior frays the group's trust; Marisol accuses her of being Cassius's informant. A shouting match ends with Marisol walking out. The beat is heartbreak — found family can break exactly because it matters so much.

chapters.title: The Audition Notice
chapters.summary: Ros's POV. Cassius announces a mandatory senior 'Legacy Audition' where students must present their 'authentic selves' — clearly designed to force Ros out. Meanwhile @hallowayghost posts again, but not from Ros. The beat is rising panic: Cassius has hijacked even his voice.

chapters.title: Impostor
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, alone in a laundromat at night. Marisol realizes the fake @hallowayghost posts are Cassius laundering his own blackmail through Ros's reputation. She photographs evidence but hesitates to return. The beat is lonely clarity — pride versus forgiveness.

chapters.title: June's Confession
chapters.summary: June's POV. June tells the group everything: what Cassius knows, what he demanded, why she complied. Instead of exile, Ros offers her the ledger pen — a place in the Locker. The beat is grace; trust rebuilt through truth rather than perfection.

chapters.title: Counter-Cipher
chapters.summary: Ros and Dev's dual POV. Using grandma's cipher, the group begins encoding their own counter-archive: receipts, screenshots, testimony from students Cassius squeezed. The beat is quiet empowerment — the Locker's original purpose restored, aimed at its corruptor.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Gym
chapters.summary: Cassius's POV, the novel's only villain chapter. Cassius catches wind of the counter-archive and sets a trap, planning to pin the entire blackmail scheme on Ros publicly at the auditions. The beat is chilling confidence — the antagonist believes he's already won.

chapters.title: Locked Out
chapters.summary: Ros's POV. The group arrives to find the Locker sealed, its contents stolen — except the one card Ros kept: grandma's original recipe. Cassius texts Ros a photo of the ledger and an ultimatum. The beat is despair at its lowest point; the legacy seems lost.

chapters.title: The Real Recipe
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Re-reading grandma's card, Marisol spots what Ros missed: the 'ingredients' list names five people, and the 'method' is a plan — distribute copies of everything before Cassius can bury it. The beat is rekindled hope; grandma planned for this.

chapters.title: Distribution Night
chapters.summary: Full ensemble POV, rapid cuts. The five execute grandma's method: seeding the counter-archive across the school's printers, projectors, and phones hours before the Legacy Audition. The beat is breathless momentum — a heist built from love instead of greed.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Ros's POV. On stage before the whole school, Cassius attempts his frame-job — but the counter-archive floods every screen behind him, and student after student stands to testify. The beat is triumphant catharsis; the audience becomes the jury, then the family.

chapters.title: When the Labels Come Off
chapters.summary: Ros's POV. In the aftermath, Cassius faces expulsion and investigation; the school board, exposed too, wobbles. Ros deletes @hallowayghost forever and, at the microphone during graduation rehearsal, introduces himself by name — Ros Winterbourne, keeper of the Locker. The beat is quiet, hard-won selfhood.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Epilogue, ensemble POV. Weeks later, the five reopen the Locker together, adding their own names to grandma's ledger and leaving the door unlocked for whoever comes next. Ros mails a letter to his grandmother's old address, telling her he's home. The beat is warm resolution: belonging isn't found, it's built — and passed on.
